Commentary.Commentary: The Sri Lankan players have made their way out to the center. Tamim Iqbal and Saif Hassan are the two openers for Bangladesh. Lakmal to begin with the ball.

Sri Lanka have declared! The Sri Lankan inning is over. They have got a lead of 107 runs. It was all due to the marathon stand between skipper Karunaratne and de Silva. Skipper Karunaratne scored 244 while de Silva got out on 166 but they ensured Sri Lanka got the lead, chasing the massive score posted by Bangladesh. Dickwell and Hasaranga ensured that the lead got over 100. A very tough for the Bangladeshi bowlers. They have bowled 179 overs in this innings and have failed to get all the 10 wickets. On Day 4, they failed to get any wicket. However, in the first session on Day 5, they managed to get 5 and then Sri Lanka have declared after going for Lunch.
... Day 5, Session 2 ...

So, the lead is over 100. Sri Lanka might fancy playing a few overs, get some quick runs and then try to force a collapse with the ball. Can they something on that sort? We will find out in the second session. Join us for the same after the Lunch break.

Another session where the bowlers had to toil hard. Sri Lanka went after the bowling and scored quick runs and lost wicket in the process. Apart form Jayed, all the bowlers who bowled got at least one wicket. Bangladesh will look to quickly close this innings in the second session.

Now, the wicket is still looking like a Day 3 wicket as there is hardly any assitance. There were expectations that this might break down on Day 4 and Day 5 but nothing of that sorts has happend here. Karunaratne and de Silva batted with eased in the first hour but got dismissed by Taskin. Dickwella and Hasaranga played handy knocks to take the lead over 100. Lakmal is batting well at the moment.

Another very good session for Sri Lanka. They have added over 100 runs this season and their lead has crossed 100 too. However, Bangladesh have got something to show this time as they have managed to bag 5 wickets. However, the game is heading towards a draw unless we get to witness something dramatic.

Dhananjaya de Silva is up for a chat. De Silva says that as an individual he is really happy with his performances. Praises skipper for the double ton. Says that the wicket was a bit tricky as a few balls were turning and a few weren't. Tells that he is doing well with the bat. Tells that he is always ready to bowl whenever the team needs him. Adds that he though enjoys batting more.

Pitch report - Farveez Maharoof is down for the pitch report. He says that the wicket still looks good for batting. Feels the spinners can do well though. Adds that if the Sri Lankan batters show intent and give their bowlers 55-60 overs to bowl out the opposition, we can have an interesting game.

Hello and welcome to the final day of the Test match between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. The game is heading towards draw unless something dramatic happens and you never keep that out of the equation. The hosts led by skipper Karunaratne's double ton and century from de Silva have got close to the Bangladeshi score. They would now look to score briskly in the first session and then maybe give a couple of sessions for the bowlers to try and bundle out Bangladesh. The possibility cannot be ruled out but for that to happen, first they need to score briskly. Doing that is not going to be easy on a Day 5 wicket. Plenty of excitement still left in the game. Let's see which way it goes.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

Right! Day 4 ends. The game is heading towards a draw. However, it is not over until it is over. If Sri Lanka can manage to get a 150-200 run lead, they can give themselves some chance. Will they be able to do so? We will find out all these on Day 5 when the action will begin. Remember that it will be an early start. The action on Day 5 will begin at 0945 local (0415 GMT). Do join us then. For now, it is goodbye from our end. Stay safe and take care.

What about bowling? Well, it was a hard toil for the bowlers. They tried hard but without any luck. More than 2 sessions and they failed to get any wicket. One can say there wasn't much for the bowlers on this wicket but credit to the two batters who just never looked in trouble. Both their main spinners have bowled 84 overs together and have managed just 2 wickets, and both of them came on Day 3. So, nothing much to talk about the bowling. They would've been happy to get back to the dressing room due to the bad light. They returned after a brief stoppage but once again nothing went their way.

The day started with the skipper Karunaratne getting to his ton. Along with de Silva, he just kept going and going. The Sri Lankan players just gave nothing away. De Silva brought up his century in the 2nd session and their marathon stand crossed 200 and then 250. They got the deficit to under 100 before bad light forced the game to stop. However, we returned after a while and the Sri Lankan skipper got to his maiden double century. De Silva brought up his 150 and the marathon stand got over 300 and the duo just kept going before the light got bad again and the game was stopped.

Okay! The final word has come. The play has been called off. STUMPS ON DAY 4. A superb day for Sri Lanka. Karunarate and de Silva have batted the entire day without losing their wicket. Sure the pitch is good to bat on, sure there is nothing for the bowler but it still is a monumental effort by these two batters.

Hang on! Some drama. Abu Jayed was ready to bowl but he gave the ball to Taskin. And the lightmeter came out again. Maybe the umpires are asking Bangladesh to not bowl Taskin who is a fast bowler. But looks like Bangladesh are not doing that. And hence, off we go again, due to bad light. Don't think we will have any further play on Day 4. Stay tuned for the update.

1206 local (0636 GMT) - The players are leaving the field for Lunch. The Sri Lankan openers have safely seen off the tricky period before the break.
